meta.description: Canonical test cases for parent-time. This is the single source of truth — every test case listed here must be implemented in every language. Each implementation translates these specifications into its native test framework.

annotationPatterns.A: Comment above the test declaration (TypeScript, Python, Ruby, Kotlin, Java, C#, Swift, Scala)
annotationPatterns.B: Trailing comment on table entries (Go, Rust)
annotationPatterns.C: Comment above or trailing on assertions (C, C++, Zig)

notes: All test cases use explicit (dateOfBirth, asOf) pairs for determinism. No test depends on the current date except where specifically noted.
When a single test covers multiple canonical IDs, list them with commas: // 1.1, 1.3
Tests that go beyond the canonical set (e.g., extra locale-specific tests) are left unannotated.

sections.title: Null / edge cases
sections.description:
These test that invalid inputs return null (or the language equivalent:
`None`, `nil`, `std::nullopt`, etc.).

The library supports ages from 0 through 500 years (6000 months). Inputs
that produce an age outside this range return null.

sections.title: Weeks+days tier (7 days to <3 calendar months)
Month boundaries — February non-leap year
sections.description: 2025 is not a leap year (Feb has 28 days).

sections.title: Month boundaries — February leap year
sections.description: 2024 is a leap year (Feb has 29 days).

sections.title: Month boundaries — leap year baby (born Feb 29)
Born-on-31st progression
sections.description:
Tracks a child born Jan 31, 2025 through their first year, verifying
month-count clamping at each step.

sections.title: Default asOf (current date)
sections.description:
Test that when `asOf` is omitted, the function uses the current date.
This requires mocking or overriding the system clock.

sections.title: ParentTime class — English locale delegation
sections.description: Verify that the class-based API produces the same results as the bare functions.

sections.title: i18n — locale with all plural features
sections.description:
Test with a locale that exercises singular/plural forms, half marker, delimiter,
justBorn label, and stage labels. The TypeScript tests use an inline
Spanish-like locale for this purpose.

sections.title: Locale-specific edge cases — plural rules
sections.description:
Test locales that exercise distinct plural rule families: Hebrew dual forms
(`he`), Macedonian mod-based plurals (`mk`), Swahili noun-class changes
(`sw`), Indonesian other-only (`id`), and Amharic zero-one rule with
Ethiopic delimiter (`am`).

sections.title: Locale lookup by code string
sections.description:
These test the `getLocale` / `get_locale` / `GetLocale` lookup function that
returns a locale object given a code string.
